SBFI species-weighted gross stem volume

Source: R/host-volume.R
sbfi_species_volume.Rd

Build a species-group volume raster (m3/ha) from the Satellite-Based Forest Inventory (SBFI) 2020 geodatabase, as stand volume (STRUCTURE_VOLUME_AVG) multiplied by the summed area share of the requested species. This mirrors the ntems_species_volume() construction, so SBFI and NTEMS volumes are directly comparable (and share a lineage).

Usage

sbfi_species_volume(
  gdb_file,
  species,
  study_area,
  res = 100,
  grid_layer = "_Grid_forested_ecosystem",
  tile_fmt = "CA_2020_tile_%d_metrics",
  filename = NULL
)

Arguments

gdb_file

character, path to the SBFI .gdb.

species

character vector of SBFI species codes, e.g. c("POPU.TRE", "POPU.BAL", "POPU.GRA").

study_area

SpatVector (or sf) polygons defining the area of interest.

res

numeric, output resolution (m) in the SBFI native CRS (default 100).

grid_layer

character, the SBFI tile-grid layer name.

tile_fmt

character, sprintf() format mapping a grid Id to its metrics layer name.

filename

(optional) character, path to write the result to.

Value

SpatRaster of species-weighted stand volume (m3/ha).

Details

Only the SBFI tiles intersecting study_area are read, and only the species / volume columns are loaded (the national geodatabase is large). Tiles are rasterized in the SBFI native CRS (no raster reprojection; the study-area vector is reprojected to the geodatabase CRS) and mosaicked. Zeros are kept (mapped forest with no target species), so the raster's non-NA extent doubles as the SBFI coverage mask.
